appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus interpellait de temps en temps un domestique : « Comment allez-vous ? Avez-vous reçu mon pneumatique ? Viendrez-vous ? »... ses habiletés tournaient contre le baron, car on trouvait extraordinaires ses amabilités si intimes et ses pneumatiques à des valets de pied. Ceux-ci en étaient, d'ailleurs, moins flattés que gênés pour leurs camarades.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's calculated, overly familiar warmth toward footmen — pneumatiques, intimate chat — is explicitly said to backfire, striking onlookers as bizarre and leaving even the footmen embarrassed rather than flattered.

appraisal_events.evidence: l'amie de Mlle Vinteuil avait dégagé, de papiers plus illisibles que des papyrus ponctués d'écriture cunéiforme, la formule éternellement vraie... Ce qu'elle avait permis, grâce à son labeur, qu'on connût de Vinteuil, c'était à vrai dire toute l'œuvre de Vinteuil.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits her years of patient, expert labor deciphering Vinteuil's illegible manuscripts with making his true, far greater body of work known at all, securing him an immortal, compensatory glory he could not have won without her.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mlle Vinteuil n'avait agi que par sadisme, ce qui ne l'excusait pas, mais j'eus plus tard une certaine douceur à le penser... j'aurais pu rétablir entre elle et le souvenir de son père une communication assez douce.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator restates that her cruelty toward her father's memory was sadism, not excused, even as his tone toward her softens into retrospective sympathy and imagined reconciliation.

appraisal_events.evidence: Je regardai la Patronne, dont l'immobilité farouche semblait protester contre les battements de mesure exécutés par les têtes ignorantes des dames du Faubourg... qu'elle ne flancherait pas à l'andante, qu'elle ne crierait pas à l'allegro.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's rigid, wordless composure during the concert is read as proof of a hardier, deeper musical understanding than the fashionable but ignorant Faubourg guests around her display.

status_effects.explanation: His calculated show of grand-seigneur familiarity with servants is read by others as strange rather than charming, undercutting rather than enhancing his standing.
Her devoted, expert work of transcription is portrayed as the sole reason Vinteuil's true greatness could be known at all, an unambiguous narratorial tribute.
Thanks to his friend's labor, what survives of Vinteuil is his true, far greater body of work, securing him a posthumous, immortal glory.
Her earlier profanation is again named as sadism and left unexcused, though the narrator's tone has grown more compassionate than condemnatory.

Her stoic containment during the concert is read as evidence of real, tested musical understanding rather than mere performance, implicitly elevating her above the merely fashionable listeners around her.

ambiguities: The narrator's softened judgment of Mlle Vinteuil coexists with an explicit refusal to excuse her, so the delta reflects the sadism charge rather than a genuine reversal into elevation.

Mme Verdurin's dignified composure in E4 partly echoes free indirect style and earlier passages have shown her musical raptures to be theatrical, so this elevation is read cautiously rather than as full narratorial endorsement.
